channel.title: Cadence Evidence — PT Research Signal
channel.description: Daily curated physical therapy & rehab research for clinicians. AI-scored signal from 56 sources.

item.title: Rehabilitation of Athletes With Hamstring Strain Injury: SONAFE-Brazil Clinical Practice Guideline.
item.description: The National Society of Sports Physical Therapy (SONAFE-Brazil) released a clinical practice guideline using the GRADE approach to inform rehabilitation outcomes in athletes with hamstring strain injury, synthesizing evidence from randomized clinical trials.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Association Between Early Postoperative Limb Symmetry Index Scores and 2-Year Patient-Reported Outcomes After Quadriceps Tendon Autograft ACL Reconstruction.
item.description: A case series of 100 patients undergoing QT-ACLR showed that early isometric quadriceps LSI at 3 months (β = 3.9; adjusted R² = 0.36; P < .03) and isokinetic quadriceps strength at 9 months (β = 3.9-4.7; adjusted R² = 0.34-0.35; P ≤ .003) were independently associated with higher 2-year IKDC and Lysholm scores.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Post burn Cubital Tunnel Syndrome Electrophysiological and Functional Responses to High intensity Laser Therapy versus Extracorporeal Shock Wave Therapy: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
item.description: A randomized controlled trial (N=75) found that both high-intensity laser therapy (HILT) and extracorporeal shock wave therapy (ESWT) combined with ulnar nerve gliding exercises (UNGE) improved nerve conduction and upper-limb function more than UNGE alone in post-burn cubital tunnel syndrome. HILT produced significantly greater improvements than ESWT in electrophysiological outcomes and DASH scores, with benefits maintained at 12-week follow-up (all P < .001).
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Percutaneous Electrolysis for the Management of Musculoskeletal Disorders. A Systematic Review With Meta-Analysis.
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis found very low-certainty evidence that adding percutaneous electrolysis (PNE) to therapeutic exercise (TE) was not superior to sham or TE alone for pain or function in tendinopathies. Low-certainty evidence showed PNE plus TE provided greater short- to medium-term pain reduction compared to dry needling plus TE in tendinopathies, but no significant differences in myofascial pain syndrome.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Reframing hands-on musculoskeletal assessment as a measurement instrument rather than a technique debate: a theoretical framework applying COSMIN to HODA-A.
item.description: This theoretical paper proposes a framework, HODA-A, for conceptualizing hands-on musculoskeletal examination as a clinician-reported outcome measurement process, aligning with COSMIN principles for construct definition, content validity, examiner calibration, and reliability/validity testing.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Effects of thoracic kinesiological taping on pulmonary functions, respiratory muscle strength, and functional independence in patients with hemiplegia: a randomized controlled clinical trial.
item.description: In a 30-patient RCT, thoracic kinesiology taping (KT) combined with conventional rehabilitation significantly improved pulmonary function (FVC, FEV1, PEF) and inspiratory muscle strength (MIP) in chronic stroke patients, with greater changes in the KT group (all p < 0.001) compared to sham taping.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Comparison of kinesio taping and myofascial release therapy in cervicogenic headache: a randomized controlled trial.
item.description: An 81-patient RCT showed that both kinesio taping (KT) and myofascial release (MFR) combined with home exercise effectively reduced pain, disability, and headache frequency in cervicogenic headache over 4 weeks. MFR provided more sustained improvements in disability and physical quality of life (p < 0.001) at one-month follow-up compared to KT.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Is Reduced Spinal Range of Motion a Prognostic Factor for Pain Intensity, Disability, and Global Recovery in People With Specific or Nonspecific Spinal Pain? A Systematic Review.
item.description: A systematic review of 37 studies found very low certainty evidence that it is unclear whether reduced spinal range of motion independently predicts pain intensity, disability, or global recovery in people with specific or nonspecific spinal pain.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Mirror therapy versus functional electrical stimulation cycling in post-stroke lower limb rehabilitation: a randomized controlled trial.
item.description: An RCT comparing mirror therapy (MT) and functional electrical stimulation-assisted cycling (FES-C) as adjuncts to conventional rehabilitation for subacute stroke found both effective, with greater improvements in FMA-LE scores compared to control (MT: MD -2.60, p=0.004; FES-C: MD -3.00, p=0.008), and FES-C also significantly improved Brunnstrom stage and SS-QOL.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Effect of iTBS and rTMS Combined with Robotic Rehabilitation on Ambulation and Lower Extremity Motor Function in Chronic SCI Patients.
item.description: A single-blind RCT (n=30) found that both rTMS and iTBS combined with robotic rehabilitation improved lower-extremity motor function (LEMS: rTMS median +4.0, iTBS +5.0 vs sham +0.0; SCIM III: rTMS +3.0, iTBS +5.0 vs sham +0.0) and ambulation (10 MWT: rTMS +6.6, iTBS +5.7 vs sham +0.7) in chronic incomplete SCI patients at 4-week follow-up, with no significant differences between active groups.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Shear wave elastography for assessing lower extremity muscle stiffness after anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction: A systematic review.
item.description: A systematic review of 6 studies (173 ACLR participants) found reduced passive vastus medialis shear modulus in operative limbs (Hedges' g -1.10 to -1.21 vs controls), associated with quadriceps strength, knee function, and landing biomechanics. Semitendinosus stiffness was reduced after hamstring tendon harvest (g -1.29 to -1.64).
item.author: PubMed

item.title: A Return to Performance Continuum for Football (Soccer) Players After ACL Reconstruction: Bridging Rehabilitation, Return to Play and Sustained Performance.
item.description: This paper outlines a staged return-to-performance continuum for football players after ACL reconstruction, emphasizing a structured transition from return-to-sport clearance to sustained performance. It integrates on-field rehabilitation, team training, competitive match play, and early/sustained return to performance through four pillars: movement quality, technical/tactical re-training, physical reconditioning, and neuromuscular performance.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Can Psychological Readiness Predict Successful Return to Sports After Patellar Stabilization Surgery in Adolescent Patients? A Retrospective Cohort Study.
item.description: A retrospective cohort study of 97 adolescent patients found that ACL-RSI scores ≥59.2 were associated with a 3.56 times increased likelihood of successful return to sport (78.3% overall) after patellar stabilization surgery, independently of sex, procedure type, or injury characteristics.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Effectiveness of office-based vergence/accommodative therapy with movement for accommodative dysfunction in concussion-related convergence insufficiency: a secondary analysis of the CONCUSS randomised clinical trial
item.description: A secondary analysis of the CONCUSS RCT found that 12 sessions of immediate office-based vergence/accommodative therapy with movement (OBVAM) and home reinforcement remediated 86% of accommodative dysfunction in concussion-related convergence insufficiency, compared to 28% in the watchful waiting group.
item.author: BJSM

item.title: Efficacy and evidence certainty of traditional Chinese exercises for musculoskeletal disorders: an umbrella review of meta-analyses
item.description: An umbrella review synthesizing 547 unique associations from meta-analyses established high-certainty evidence for traditional Chinese exercises (TCEs), especially Tai Chi, in improving physical function in knee osteoarthritis, mental health in neck pain, and sleep quality in fibromyalgia. Optimal benefits were achieved with sustained interventions of ≥6 months duration, ≥3 times/week frequency, and ≥150 min weekly volume.
item.author: BJSM

item.title: Identifying heterogeneous patterns of real-world upper limb use beyond motor severity: a cross-sectional sensor-based study in people with subacute stroke
item.description: A cross-sectional study of 101 subacute stroke patients identified six heterogeneous upper limb activity patterns beyond motor severity using accelerometers and clinical assessments. Key distinguishing factors included motor function tests (ARAT), Motor Activity Log, upper limb inattention, and paretic-side dominance, suggesting personalized rehabilitation should consider factors beyond motor deficits.
item.author: J NeuroEng Rehabil

item.title: The Role of Psychosocial Factors in Returning to Physical Activity and Sport Among Female Football Players After Anterior Cruciate Ligament Injury: A Scoping Review
item.description: A scoping review of seven studies found that psychosocial factors significantly influence female football players' return to physical activity and sport after ACL injury. Barriers included uncertainty, fear, lack of confidence, and poor social support, while facilitators were confidence, motivation, strong social support, and athletic identity.
item.author: Sports Med - Open

item.title: Physiotherapists' perspectives on direct access in a referral-based system in Austria - A qualitative study.
item.description: A qualitative study in Austria explored physiotherapists' perspectives on direct access, revealing perceived readiness for triage roles despite lacking a legal framework, moderate-to-high confidence in differential diagnosis but lower in red-flag screening, and identified needs for targeted training and interprofessional collaboration.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Post-concussion screen time duration and type and its association with symptom resolution in youth aged 11-17 years
item.description: A cohort study in youth (11-17 years old) found that optimal median screen time of 141 min/day during the first 3 days post-concussion was associated with a 1.35-fold higher rate of symptom resolution compared to 260 min/day. Those with 120-240 min/day of screen time had 2.27-fold faster symptom resolution than those with <120 min/day and 1.58-fold faster resolution than those with >240 min/day.
item.author: BJSM

item.title: Over-the-counter analgesics improve postconcussion symptoms and recovery: findings from the Concussion Assessment, Research and Education (CARE) Consortium
item.description: A cohort study from the CARE Consortium found that concussion patients using OTC analgesics had a 24.5% higher rate of return to unrestricted play and 30.3% lower SCAT-3 symptom scores compared to non-users. Early use was associated with a 35.6% higher rate of return to unrestricted play.
item.author: BJSM
